chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Mu'adhi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi al-Hamadani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hasan ibn Fuddal, on the authority of his father, from al-Rida Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them both), saying:

I asked him about the word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Do they wait but that Allah should come to them in the shadow of the clouds along with the angels?' He (AS) said: 'It means: Do they wait but that Allah should send angels to them in the shadow of the clouds,' and thus it was revealed.
ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Allah should come to them in the shadow of the clouds' mean in Shia tafsir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the phrase 'Allah should come to them' in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:210) signifies the descent of angels in the shadow of clouds, rather than a literal physical descent of God. This interpretation aligns with the grammatical structure and reinforces the concept of divine manifestation through angels, a key theme in Shia exegesis.
